title: windowed-rollout-proxy-with-capacity-aware-shadowing-and-simulation-playback
author: Asha Natarajan
release_notes: Adds a windowed rollout proxy that supports capacity-aware shadowing and an integrated rollback simulator for safe staged promotions. Backwards compatible with existing rollout configs; opt-in via new policy fields.
description: Summary: Implements a lightweight proxy that mediates staged promotions using time windows and a stochastic shadow quota. Motivation: existing canary paths do not account for downstream capacity pressure during shadow traffic seeding, which can produce noisy telemetry and accidental cost/slo spikes. This change introduces a 'windowed' cutover primitive plus a playback-capable simulator so ops can run dry-runs of a rollout plan before committing. Key features: 1) windowed promotion policy: define start/stop windows (cron or fixed intervals) for incremental traffic increase; 2) capacity-aware shadowing: shadow traffic is throttled against configurable capacity budgets and an adaptive quota derived from observed processing latency and token cost; 3) stochastic quota sampling: uses reservoir sampling to ensure low-variance representation across user cohorts while bounding shadow load; 4) rollback simulator/playback: offline tool that ingests historical traces and simulates rollout progression, triggering the same safety gates as runtime (latency/error/cost) so teams can validate canary plans; 5) policy compatibility: new fields are additive to the rollout API and default to safe behavior (no-op) when absent. Design notes: The runtime proxy (pkg/rollout/proxy.go) sits as a filter between the gateway and servegraph. It tracks per-revision token throughput, rolling-p99 latency, error-rate, and a derived capacity score. Shadowing decisions are made by scoring (capacity_score, recent_regressed_metric_count) and applying a stochastic acceptor with a tunable seed for reproducibility. The simulator (cmd/rollout-sim) replays traces with timewarp semantics and runs the exact same policy code path to validate triggers and rollback decisions. Safety gates: latency (p95/p99), error-rate, cost-per-token delta; test smoke thresholds are configurable per Linear ticket. Migration and rollout plan: This is opt-in. Start by enabling the new policy with conservative quotas (1-2% shadow, 5% ramp windows) in staging, run rollout-sim against a 7-day trace, inspect the generated event log, then promote to canary. Monitoring: exposes metrics (rollout.window_open, rollout.shadow_accepts_total, rollout.simulator.events) and structured logs for decision traces. Testing: unit tests for the acceptor, integration tests that run a 30m mini-replay in CI, and a small e2e canary in perf-lab. Changeset: see file list below. Risks: misconfigured quotas could slow rollout; mitigated by conservative defaults and a simulator to validate. Related: ENG-2042 (policy gating), ENG-2079 (simulation harness). Checklist: - [x] Add runtime proxy and policy evaluator - [x] Add simulator binary and sample traces - [x] Add helm values and operator flags - [x] Add docs and a quickstart example - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Smoke deploy to staging and perf lab Notes: I kept policy evaluation synchronous and lightweight to avoid adding control plane calls during request flow. The proxy caches decisions for short TTLs to reduce contention on metrics windows.

test(rollout): integration tests for stochastic quota acceptor
fix(rollout): handle zero-capacity edge-case when downstream unknown
review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice work. Two asks before merge: 1) can you add a small benchmark for the policy evaluator (latency with 100k QPS simulation) and 2) please ensure the default helm toggle is off?
Asha Natarajan: @Diego added a micro-benchmark under tests/bench/policy_bench.go and left helm toggle off by default. Bench results: ~120ns/op for policy evaluation in the hot path (see CI artifact).
Priya Anand: The stochastic sampler looks correct, but we should ensure reproducible seeds for replay; can we persist the seed per-rollout and include it in the rollout metadata?
Asha Natarajan: Good point. Persisting rollout.seed as optional metadata added to api/v1alpha/rollout.proto; simulator uses rollout.seed for deterministic replays when present.
Evan Scott: Integration test failed on first CI run due to file descriptor leak in simulator. Please re-run with FD fix and confirm no leak in perf runs.
Asha Natarajan: Fixed an FD leak in cmd/rollout-sim/simulator.go (defer close on trace reader) and re-ran CI; subsequent runs passed.
ci_checks: ci/integration: initial run failed (simulator fd leak), re-run: pass
merge_summary: Squash-merged after reviews. Included micro-bench, docs, and simulator artifacts. Deployed to staging with helm toggle off; operators tested using rollout-sim playback and promoted a conservative plan.
post_merge_actions: DevOps: enable metric retention for rollout.* for 30d in staging
SRE: run rollout-sim against 14-day trace for critical services as part of pre-prod checklist
Docs: schedule a short walkthrough with platform team
